# v0.3.52 — Digest links come from the feed

**Upgrading from 0.3.51:**

- Rebuild and recreate the app container (`docker compose up -d --build alexclaw-prod`). No configuration or database change.
- `rss_collector` now hands on JSON items instead of text blocks: `{"items": [{"feed", "title", "summary", "link"}], "skipped": [{"feed", "url"}]}`. A custom workflow whose prompt parsed the old `**Feed**: title` blocks gets a list of items instead.
- Digests cite their sources as links taken from the feed. When `llm_transform` receives a list of items with links, the model sees the items numbered and without URLs, cites them by number, and each citation becomes a link to that item. Stored prompts need no change.
- `telegram_notify` gains a `link_preview` option: `"link_preview": false` turns off the preview card Telegram adds for a link. The `parse_mode` option it used to advertise was never read, and is no longer offered.

## Changes

- `rss_collector`'s summaries are plain text: the description's HTML is removed before it is shortened to 300 characters. The executor's sanitizer read the old text output as one HTML document, which flattened the items and let a description cut inside a link swallow the next item.
- `llm_transform` removes any link or URL the model writes in a summary of feed items, and drops a citation number that matches no item. Feed text cannot put a link with a scheme or `www.` into the message; a bare domain quoted from a feed can still appear as text (see SECURITY.md). Items without a summary (`rss_fetch`'s) give their description as plain text.
- `telegram_notify` renders Markdown links as Telegram links. The link text and the URL are escaped, and only `http` and `https` URLs become links.
